title: Bit-identical warp, register and prefetch schedules do not recover the rest of the MTP3 decode round
question: Can schedule-only changes that keep every output byte recover the 1.40 ms (8.7%) of the RTX 5090 MTP3 round that EXP-055 left above 90% of the bandwidth floor, and does the RTX 4090 have its own sm_89 wins?
answer: No. Nsight Compute and four private-launcher sweeps (1,631 byte-identical rows per pass on the RTX 5090, 449 on the RTX 4090) found no T=4 schedule that beats production beyond noise for the Q4/Q5 projections or the GDN record and fold, and an L2 hand-off prefetch only speeds a cold consumer: with the whole weight resident in L2 the mixer still takes 16.4 us, and in the production graph it already takes 16.6 us, so the projections are issue-bound and prefetch has nothing left to hide. The one surviving candidate, a two-warp BF16 attention CTA for the group of six above the 16K split tier, cut the in-graph attention partial by 6.1% at 26K but moved decode only +0.3% to +0.9% from 26K to 60K, while its public op curve regressed 3.7-5.4% between 16,387 and 20,000 keys, a band the graph bucket cannot route around. By exclusive time (PDL lets GDN query/key overlap value/z by 4.4 us per call) the projections' recoverable remainder is 1.15 ms (7.2%), and closing it needs a different accumulation order. Outside the projections, the traced 26K round also spends 0.47 ms in 297 small normalization and gating kernels, 0.17 ms in 815 kernel-boundary gaps (median 0.22 us) and 0.34 ms in host round trips around the verify result and the next round's inputs; these shares keep every byte but are fusion and serving-loop work, not kernel schedules.
decision: Reject every EXP-056 candidate on both lanes; no v0.8.2. Production stays on v0.6.10-qwen38-5090-beta.1 and the RTX 4090 lane on v0.6.8-qwen38-4090-beta.1. The projection remainder is a numerics question (a Q5 small-T tensor-core route); the bit-identical shares left are epilogue fusion of the normalization and gating kernels and keeping MTP rounds on the device.

limits: The private sweeps time isolated kernels with a cold L2. At 26K the in-graph attention partial (-6.1%) agrees with the isolated sweep (-6.2%), while the public op, which adds the append and combine kernels, moves only -2.4%.
No end-to-end point lies between 16,387 and 26,000 keys, where the op curve regresses and then recovers; the graph routes that whole band with the envelope of its 16,385-32,762 bucket.
The first baseline arm read 1.9% faster than the last at the seed context. Below 16,385 keys the two builds run identical kernels, so the short-context deltas are run-order drift.
The RTX 4090 CUDA event timer resolves 1.024 us, so its best T=4 leads (1-2 ticks) are at the resolution limit, and no in-graph RTX 4090 trace was taken.
The GDN fold's T>=2 isolated timings are bimodal (about 215 or 410 us, independent of schedule across passes); in the graph the fold costs 0.168 ms per round, below the isolated cold floor.
